provenance.warning: Aggregates transcribed from screenshot; no independent re-execution

active.name: GLPK
active.formula: min Σᵢ cᵢwᵢ + λΣᵢ|wᵢ − pᵢ|, subject to Σᵢwᵢ=1 and 0≤wᵢ≤capᵢ
active.impact: Reference placement used to compare carbon intensity, operating price, weighted latency, modeled risk and allocation-weighted APY. No simulated quantum circuit.

active.name: Quantum Oracle (Grover)
principles: 128 candidates per register; 32 Born-rule measurements each
Classical objective-aware candidate sorting and encoding
active.formula: Oτ|z⟩ = (−1)^[E(z)≤τ]|z⟩; D=2|s⟩⟨s|−I; choose best of measured feasible allocations
active.impact: Independent candidate allocations feed environmental, operating and treasury metrics. In the 200-case run all displayed averages matched GLPK, which requires a full allocation-level audit; zero recorded fallbacks does not prove quantum advantage.

active.name: Curvilinear Quantum Fusion
principles: Two depth-3 measured circuit runs per worker
Quintic curved energy schedule and XY exchange mixing
Adaptive Grover thresholds over 252 weight-five basis states
active.formula: s(t)=10t³−15t⁴+6t⁵; U≈Πₗe^(−iγₗHcost)e^(−iβₗHXY); select best measured state
active.impact: Produces a separate 20-region allocation; changes blended carbon, cost, weighted latency, risk and illustrative regional yield. Hybrid because objective-aware encoding and selection remain classical.

active.name: Adaptive Grover 10q
principles: Three rounds of adaptive Grover marking
Cost-aware allocation decoder and classical outcome selection
active.impact: Generates region weights from simulated quantum measurements. Those weights change the same output statistics as the other independent engines.

active.name: Geometry-Aware Quantum Walk
principles: Grover marking with a nonlinear schedule
active.impact: Studies constraint-preserving circuit mixing and its effect on allocation risk/carbon/cost versus GLPK, without a classical optimal-allocation fallback.

retired.name: Standard QAOA + GLPK
retired.aspect: Quantum gate-based candidate proposal with classical GLPK refinement and quality guard
retired.reason: 200/200 GLPK fallbacks; zero gap therefore not independent quantum achievement.

retired.name: Fluid XY-QAOA + GLPK
retired.formula: U = Πₗ exp(−iβₗ HXY) exp(−iγₗ Hcost), HXY=Σ(XᵢXⱼ+YᵢYⱼ)/2
retired.aspect: 5-region one-hot microbatches, XY mixer, guarded GLPK residual refinement; separate IBM microcircuit hardware evidence
retired.reason: 200/200 GLPK fallbacks in this run; IBM microcircuit validation does not establish full-system quantum advantage.

retired.name: Gaseous QAOA + GLPK
retired.aspect: X-mixer QAOA with gas-inspired classical Boltzmann reweighting and GLPK residual solve
retired.reason: 200/200 GLPK fallbacks; same solution as GLPK and slower.

retired.name: A*-Guided Four-Technique Ensemble
retired.aspect: Classical A* controller plus simulated Grover, quantum walks, annealing and minimum-finding heuristics; 4×7 qubits
retired.reason: 19.84% gap in user 200-case run; older 1.62% came from a different benchmark formulation.

retired.name: Adiabatic Quantum Engine
retired.aspect: Digitized adiabatic evolution using 7-qubit statevector simulation, without GLPK solution injection
retired.reason: Very large 270.91% objective gap in latest same-case comparison.

retired.name: Geometry XY-Only
retired.aspect: 10-qubit, depth-3 XY quantum walk with conserved Hamming weight
retired.reason: Worse gap than retained geometry variants on 200 shared scenarios.

earlier.name: Initial Quantum Ensemble v130–v131
earlier.formula: E(w) = Σᵢ cᵢwᵢ + λΣᵢ|wᵢ−pᵢ|; quantum phases and walks act on 128 simulated basis states
earlier.aspect: Independent Grover, walks, annealing and minimum-finding research; persistent 7-qubit workers
earlier.benchmark: v130 reported 42.11% mean gap and 275.94 ms median; v131 warm execution median 1.61 ms on its local test (different experimental conditions).

earlier.name: A*-Guided Ensemble without analytical fallback
earlier.formula: A*: f(s) = g(s) + h(s); E(w) = Σᵢcᵢwᵢ + λΣᵢ|wᵢ−pᵢ|
earlier.aspect: Graph frontier with four quantum-inspired sampling operators; analytic LP fallback removed in v133
earlier.benchmark: v133 measured 8.16% mean gap and 1.20 ms median vs SciPy HiGHS in 32 synthetic cases; v132 prior 0%-like result was attributable to classical analytical fallback.

earlier.name: Independent Ensemble v134 (separate LP study)
earlier.formula: Grover + quantum walks + annealing-style phases + A* frontier; min E(w)
earlier.aspect: 4 × 7-qubit CPU statevector batches; no analytical fallback
earlier.benchmark: 1.62% mean gap · 32 synthetic cases · SciPy HiGHS reference; not directly comparable with the 200-case GLPK run.

earlier.name: Adiabatic Hamiltonian-only research
earlier.formula: H(s) = (1−s)Hdriver + sHcost; U ≈ Πₗ exp(−i Δt H(sₗ))
earlier.aspect: 4×7-qubit digitized adiabatic statevectors, objective-independent sampling; GLPK not used as fallback
earlier.benchmark: 43.06% mean objective gap and 1.61 ms median vs separate SciPy HiGHS LP study; not the 200-case GLPK dataset.

earlier.name: Cost-aware Grover Oracle tuning
earlier.formula: Grover G = (2|s⟩⟨s|−I)Oτ with cost-aware classical candidate scores
earlier.aspect: Four 7-qubit registers, depth 3, cost-aware classical encoding and candidate sampling
earlier.benchmark: v137 3.84% and v138 3.68% mean objective gaps vs SciPy HiGHS on their separate 32-case synthetic runs.

earlier.name: Quantum-Native Hamiltonian Oracle v139–v141
earlier.formula: H(s)=(1−s)Hdriver + sHcost; Grover Oτ and Dicke/XY mixing
earlier.benchmark: v139 11.35%, v140 9.28%, v141 8.59% mean gaps on their separate 32-case synthetic HiGHS studies.

earlier.name: Quantum Oracle Research v136–v142
earlier.aspect: Grover objective oracle, 4 × 7 qubits, candidate generation and 32 shots/register in v142
earlier.benchmark: v136 11.04%, v142 3.44% mean gaps in separate synthetic LP studies; 200-case run shows near-zero reported gap and exact matched rounded KPIs.

earlier.name: Quantum contribution ablation
earlier.formula: Grover G=(2|s⟩⟨s|−I)Oτ versus uniform random candidate selection
earlier.aspect: Compared cost-aware candidate preparation with and without simulated Grover marking
earlier.benchmark: Across 32 synthetic scenarios, Grover tied classical sampling in 20 and was better in 12; average random-to-pool-best gap ~0.0027%. No proven quantum advantage.

earlier.name: Geometry-Aware research series
earlier.aspect: 10-qubit depth-3 Geometry, XY-only, Grover-only and Curvilinear Fusion research with CPU statevectors
earlier.benchmark: v146 holdout mean gap: geometry 1.41%, Grover-only 1.38%; v147 Fusion 1.43% on 48 different holdout cases vs SciPy HiGHS; 200-case GLPK gaps are separately reported above.

earlier.name: Discrete Quantum Scheduler v144
earlier.formula: min Σw,c,t x(w,c,t) C(w,c,t) + migration penalties; x∈{0,1}
earlier.aspect: Binary multi-workload placement, beam search, Grover-style and phase-walk quantum simulation
earlier.benchmark: 2.59% gap, 103.67 ms median for 8 synthetic 20-workload cases vs HiGHS MIP; classical greedy matched quality faster.
